newsitem.title: USA: BRE-X gold reserves appear overstated.
newsitem.headline: BRE-X gold reserves appear overstated.

text.p: Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc said Wednesday it has been advised by BRE-X Minerals Ltd that gold reserves claimed for the Busang II and Busang III areas of East Kalimantan, Indonesia, appear to have been overstated.
Freeport Copper also said an incomplete analyses of cores from seven holes it drilled in the Busang II area indicates insifnigicant amounts of gold.
The company said it informed BRE-X of these findings at a meeting in Jakarta on March 26.

Wednesday, Freeport Copper said, it was informed by BRE-X that, based on the recommendation of BRE-X's independent technical consultants, BRE-X was undertaking a review that includes drilling additional core holes in the Busang II area.

"In addition, BRE-X advised FCX that its independent technical consultants had informed BRE-X that there appears to be a strong possibility that the potential gold resources on the Busang project as previously reported by BRE-X have been overstated because of invalid samples and assaying of these samples."
Freeport Copper said it will monitor and cooperate with the on-going review and drilling at the Busang project.

Under the terms of its agreement with BRE-X and Indonesian interests, Freeport Copper has the right to participate as a 15 percent owner of the Busang project by paying 25 percent of the total cost of delineating a proven reserve and constructing the initial Busang complex, up to $400 million.
The company pointed out this agreement is subject to completion of due diligence satisfactory to Freeport Copper.
The company said it "will elect to participate in the development of the Busang project only if development is, in FCX's opinion, economically feasible."
